title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 8th District
area: Southern Piedmont North Carolina, including all of Anson, Montgomery, Richmond, Scotland, Stanly, and Union counties and portions of Cabarrus, Mecklenburg, and Robeson counties (Union County/southeast Charlotte suburbs).

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Mark Harris advanced unopposed. Colby Watson won a three-way Democratic primary with 47.9% of the vote.

Harris previously won the Republican nomination for North Carolina's 9th District in 2018, but no candidate was certified as the winner of that November 2018 general election; Harris was elected to the newly numbered 8th District in 2024 after the state's congressional map was redrawn.

summary.text: Mark Harris is the Republican incumbent for North Carolina's 8th Congressional District, a former Baptist pastor who was elected to the U.S. House in 2024. He previously ran unsuccessfully for U.S. Senate in 2014 and for the U.S. House in 2016, and was the Republican candidate in the 2018 race for the 9th District, a result the State Board of Elections did not certify. In Congress he serves on the Agriculture, Judiciary, and Education and Workforce Committees.

background.text: Born and raised in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, the youngest of five children, according to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; graduated from R.J. Reynolds High School.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Appalachian State University (1987) and, according to his House website, a Master of Divinity and a Doctor of Ministry from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary.
Worked as a pastor in North Carolina and Georgia, including as senior pastor of First Baptist Church in Charlotte for over a decade, according to his House website and survey responses.

Served as president of the Baptist State Convention of North Carolina from 2011 to 2013, and has served as a trustee of Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary and on the board of directors of the Biblical Recorder.

Ran in the 2014 Republican U.S. Senate primary (third, with 17.5 percent, behind Thom Tillis and Greg Brannon) and the 2016 Republican primary for the 9th District, where he trailed incumbent Robert Pittenger by 133 votes after a recount.

Won the 2018 Republican primary in the 9th District over Pittenger, and led Democrat Dan McCready by 905 votes in unofficial general-election returns. The State Board of Elections did not certify the result after questions about absentee-ballot irregularities in Bladen and Robeson counties; Harris called for a new election during a January 2019 hearing and did not run in the September 2019 special election. WBTV reports no charges were filed against Harris in the related probe.

Entered the 8th District race in September 2023 after Rep. Dan Bishop announced a run for attorney general; won the 2024 general election over Democrat Justin Dues, 59.6 percent to 40.4 percent, and took office January 3, 2025.

Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture, the Committee on the Judiciary (Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust Subcommittee; Constitution and Limited Government Subcommittee), and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress.

One bill he introduced, requiring the U.S. Attorney General to publish the names of jurisdictions that release people charged with violent crimes without cash bail, passed the House in the current session, according to WFAE.
According to his House website, he is married to Beth, and they have three adult children and eleven grandchildren.

priorities.text: Wants to reduce regulatory burdens on farmers and champion agricultural policy as a member of the House Agriculture Committee.
priorities.quote: Congressman Harris is committed to advancing policies that reduce regulatory burdens, promote innovation, and empower the agricultural sector.

priorities.text: Supports cutting taxes and regulation for small businesses and opposes new government programs to grow the economy.
priorities.quote: A strong economy starts with free enterprise, low taxes, and hard work—not more government programs.

priorities.text: Wants to return control of education to states and local communities rather than the federal government.
priorities.quote: It's time to return control of education to the states and local communities, as our Founders intended.

positions.summary: Says he will resist efforts to undermine gun rights, describing the right to bear arms as not negotiable.
positions.quote: Congressman Harris remains steadfast in defending Americans' constitutional right to self-defense, resisting any efforts to undermine this fundamental freedom.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Agriculture (Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture; Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry; General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit), the Committee on the Judiciary, and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.name: Colby Watson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 47.9% of the vote over two challengers.

summary.text: Colby Watson is the Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 8th Congressional District, a small business owner and Union County native running for office for the first time. He says he built a business with his brother that grew to employ more than 50 people. He describes his campaign as focused on ending corruption and money in politics, along with housing, health care costs, and farming.

background.text: Born in Indian Trail, North Carolina, within the 8th District; describes himself in his Ballotpedia survey as a lifelong North Carolinian, born and raised there.
Earned a high school diploma through homeschooling; WFAE reports he says he does not hold "a fancy degree."
Works as a small business owner. According to WFAE, he describes his work as a federal contractor and says he built a business with his brother that "grew to employ more than 50 people."
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 47.9 percent of the vote over Kevin Clark and Jesse Oppenheim; he has not previously held elected office.
Describes himself as a husband and father; WFAE describes him as a father of two.

priorities.text: Wants to end the influence of super PACs and corporate lobbyists in politics.
priorities.quote: Our democracy has been hijacked by big money and special interests. I'm running to restore power to the people by ending the influence of super PACs and corporate lobbyists.

priorities.text: Wants to address the cost-of-living crisis and growing wealth inequality by investing in communities, schools, healthcare, and infrastructure.
priorities.quote: The cost of living keeps rising while wages stay the same, forcing working families to do more with less.

positions.summary: In a WSOC-TV candidate questionnaire, said he supports increasing housing supply and modernizing building regulations so more homes can be built.
positions.quote: On housing, that means increasing supply and modernizing building regulations so more homes can actually be built, while also restricting corporate ownership from dominating the single-family housing market.

positions.summary: In a WSOC-TV candidate questionnaire, said he supports moving toward a universal coverage framework and expanding Medicare drug-price negotiation.
positions.quote: I support expanding Medicare’s authority to negotiate drug prices, prohibiting medical debt from appearing on credit reports, and moving toward a universal coverage framework so that getting sick never means financial collapse.

positions.summary: In a WSOC-TV candidate questionnaire, said the U.S. should not provide weapons that enable violations of international law and that he believes Israel's government and military have committed serious human rights violations in Gaza.
positions.quote: The United States should not provide weapons that enable violations of international law.

positions.summary: In a WSOC-TV candidate questionnaire, said he opposes the means and methods of the current immigration crackdown, while supporting border screening technology, additional personnel and enforcement focused on trafficking networks, smuggling and repeat violent offenders.
positions.quote: I am not in favor of the means and methods President Trump has used in his crackdown on illegal immigration.

candidates.name: Bo Whitehead

summary.text: Bo Whitehead is the Green Party candidate for North Carolina's 8th Congressional District and a first-time candidate who works as a warehouse supervisor. According to WFAE, he moved to the Charlotte area about three years ago from Georgia. He says he wants to represent the working class.

background.text: Described by WFAE as 33 years old and a warehouse supervisor who lived in Georgia before moving to the Charlotte area about three years ago; lives in Pineville.
Says in a WFAE questionnaire that he was homeschooled, received a GED, and holds prior CDL and Hazmat transport certifications.
Has no previous experience in elected office; says he is the primary caretaker for his wife.

priorities.text: Raising the minimum wage and workers' rights.
Abolishing ICE and overhauling the immigration system.
Ending wars and combating human trafficking and exploitation.

positions.summary: On his campaign site, lists a $25 minimum wage among his workers' rights priorities.
On his campaign site, says universal healthcare must be implemented as soon as possible.
positions.quote: Universal healthcare, universal childcare, and a complete overhaul of our mental health system must be implemented as soon as possible.

positions.summary: On his campaign site, says universal childcare must be implemented as soon as possible.
positions.quote: Universal healthcare, universal childcare, and a complete overhaul of our mental health system must be implemented as soon as possible.

positions.summary: On his campaign site, calls for ending ICE and overhauling the immigration system.
positions.quote: End ICE and completely rehaul our immigration system.

statements.quote: We must expand wind and solar power to update our power grid, and work towards developing a proper infostructure for electric vehicles.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions drawn from his campaign website; he has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia survey. No news questionnaires or debate coverage found.
